POV: The intersection between fear and courage

There is something beautiful about taking what is familiar and having the courage to imagine it differently.

This Strawberry Tiramisu is a playful adaptation of a traditional recipe. It keeps the essence of a classic, while allowing it to evolve into something different and special. I love to experiment, to develop recipes and see where they can go, because sometimes you simply have to trust the process.

When I look back at some of the biggest decisions of my life, so many of them required that same trust. Moving to Dubai, marrying my husband after a very short courtship, starting a blog without knowing where it would lead, and eventually building my businesses. They were all dreams of mine in one way or another, but I could never have planned exactly how or when they would happen. Somehow, the opportunities found their way to me at the right time, and I was brave enough to say yes.

But there were other opportunities that came knocking, and I wasn’t always brave enough to open the door.

When I was 26, I was offered an opportunity to develop a property in Costa Rica. It probably sounds completely out of left field, but I’ve always had a passion for real estate and development. I still sometimes wonder, what if? At the time, though, I didn’t believe I was capable of doing it. Fear and self-doubt answered for me before I had even given myself the chance to explore what might have been.

Years later, I was offered an incredible opportunity to reimagine a chain of Persian restaurants in Bahrain and create a signature restaurant in Saudi Arabia. Again, I said no. Beneath all the practical reasons, the truth was much simpler: I was scared.

Looking back, I realise how many of my decisions have existed somewhere between fear and courage. There were times I trusted myself enough to step into the unknown, and those decisions changed the course of my life. And there were other times when fear won.

I am forever a student of life. And I’m learning that courage doesn’t necessarily mean being without fear. Sometimes it simply means trusting yourself enough to move forward despite it.

results.transcript: There's something beautiful about taking something familiar and having the courage to imagine it differently. This strawberry tiramisu is exactly that, a playful twist on a classic, keeping the essence of something I love while making room for something new. And I think there are moments in life when we're asked to do the same, to trust what's unfolding even when we don't quite know where it will lead. Looking back, some of my best decisions I've made have come from the courage to step into the unknown, saying yes to opportunities before I had the answers, trusting my instincts and allowing life to surprise me. And then, there were those opportunities I let pass by because I was simply afraid. At the time, I probably had a hundred reasons why. But looking back, I can recognize when fear was making the decision for me. I don't regret those moments. They were lessons I needed to learn too. I'm learning that courage isn't the absence of fear. It's trusting yourself enough to open the door anyway.
